newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's August fishmeal output rises 79 percent.
newsitem.headline: Peru's August fishmeal output rises 79 percent.

text.p: Peru produced 25,100 tonnes of fishmeal in August, up 79 percent from the same month last year, the government said Friday.
A Fisheries' Ministry report also said fishmeal production in the first eight months of the year was 1.178 million tonnes, down 10.6 percent versus the same period last year.

Despite the large monthly rise in August's output, exports of fishmeal for the month only edged up 200 tonnes to 114,800 tonnes, compared with August last year. Exports for the first eight months were down 25.6 percent to 1.110 million tonnes, compared with the same period the year before.

The fishing sector's production was restricted in August due to a ban on anchovy fishing that started August 12. The ban in most of the country's territorial waters is to protect the species - used to make fishmeal and fish oil - during its reproductive period.
Industry officials have blamed fishing bans and sudden temperature changes in the sea for the overall fall in fishing output this year.
Fishmeal, Peru's most important fishing product, accounted for 60 percent of Peru's total processing of 41,700 tonnes of fish and other sea products in August.

Production of Peru's second most important fish product, raw fish oil, was 4,200 tonnes in August, three times its production in same month last year. Output of raw fish oil in the first eight months was 281,100 tonnes, 7.4 percent lower than in the same period last year.
In August, the total catch of Peruvian fish and sea species was up 28.2 percent to 163,200 tonnes compared with the same month last year.
The catch of anchovy, which is used to make fishmeal and fish oil, was 38,000 tonnes in August, compared to a negligible catch in the same month last year.

Peru produced 1.774 million tonnes of fishmeal in 1995, down 24.1 percent from the 2.338 million tonnes processed the previous year. However, the value of fishmeal exports last year rose 4.1 percent to $766.54 million despite an 18.2 percent drop in the volume sold abroad to 1,860,200 tonnes.

Officials have said the country's fishing production has fallen due to extended seasonal fishing bans and climatic factors while higher world prices for fishmeal have allowed a hike in the value of exports.
Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress in September he expects the fishing industry to grow by five percent next year as the climate returns to show its normal behavior.
